title: Session Galaxy vs Slotline: latency & cost comparison (sketch)
content:
Summary:
This is a working sketch comparing two internal serving philosophies for sessionized LLM workloads: the experimental Session Galaxy affinity model and our Slotline multiplexing baseline. The goal: characterize p50/p90/p99 latency, sustained throughput, and $/1M tokens for a representative chat workload (mix of short interactions and multi-turn sessions).

High-level takeaway (early):
- Session Galaxy reduces tail latency (p99) for long-lived sessions at modest cost increase for steady-state due to reduced KV cache misses.
- Slotline provides higher aggregate throughput and lower $/token at high concurrency but exhibits wider latency tails during microburst mixes.

Experiment setup (short):
- Time window: 30m runs, repeated 6x for variance.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (core pool) and T4-edge nodes simulated for edge mix.
- Model: open-7B-v2 (float16 path) and compact-quant (4-bit) variant for cost sensitivity.
- Workload: synthetic sessionized chat generator with 3 session types:
  * Micro: 1-2 turns, 15–50 tokens per turn (60% of requests)
  * Conversational: 6–12 turns, 40–150 tokens per turn (30%)
  * Longform: 20–40 turns, 200+ tokens on average (10%)
- Client concurrency: stepped 0 -> 12k rps sustained, with injected microbursts (3x for 15s every 90s).
- Key knobs: batching policy (dynbatch vs smallbatch), KV prefetch (on/off), admission control thresholds.

Cost model used:
- On-demand GPU cost normalized to $/1M tokens using measured tokens emitted. Accounting included amortized idle time for prewarmed slots and GPU-second cost for KV cache memory. Network and infra overhead estimated at +8% of base GPU cost.

Observed numeric snapshot (median of runs):
- Session Galaxy (default affinity + prefetch):
  * p50 gen latency: 28 ms
  * p90 gen latency: 86 ms
  * p99 gen latency: 310 ms
  * sustained throughput: 4.1k qps on A100 pool (7B f16)
  * kv cache hit rate: 78% overall (90% for conversational sessions)
  * $/1M tokens: $72 (baseline quantized variant $53)

- Slotline (slotized multiplexing baseline):
  * p50 gen latency: 22 ms
  * p90 gen latency: 120 ms
  * p99 gen latency: 720 ms
  * sustained throughput: 5.3k qps on same pool
  * kv cache hit rate: 48% overall (60% for conversational sessions)
  * $/1M tokens: $49 (quantized variant $37)

ASCII visualizations (text charts):
- Latency CDF sketch (p50/p90/p99 points):
  Session Galaxy: [50]---[90]----------[99]
  Slotline:        [50]--[90]----------------------[99]
  (Short: Galaxy shifts and compresses tail)

- Cost vs latency quick grid (qualitative):
  Lower cost <- Slotline -----|----- Session Galaxy -> Higher tail SLAs

Detailed notes and interpretation:
1) Tail behavior drivers:
   - Slotline uses denser multiplexing. Under bursty arrivals, some slots see request queuing and cold KV regeneration leading to long tails (observed p99 spikes to 700+ ms).
   - Session Galaxy pins session-affine execution to reduce KV churn; warm caches reduce worst-case decoding time. The tradeoff is fewer colocated requests per GPU, increasing amortized GPU-second cost.

2) Workload slicing matters:
   - For products with high fraction of short micro-interactions (e.g., quick suggestions), Slotline's higher throughput and lower median latency are attractive.
   - For long conversational experiences (customer support, coding assistants), Session Galaxy meaningfully improves user-perceived stability.

3) Batching and admission impact:
   - Dynamic batching with an aggressive token/latency cap reduces Slotline p90 but doesn't fully close p99 gap.
   - Small-batch mode (favoring low latency) reduces median for both but increases $/token significantly.

Operational considerations:
- SLO carve-outs: consider per-route routing policies where critical routes (chat sessions > 8 turns) default to Galaxy; bulk embeddings or short completions use Slotline.
- Autoscaling: Galaxy needs more conservative scale-up to avoid saturation-induced queueing—provisioning buffer should be larger by ~15–20% compared to Slotline.
- Fallbacks: implement automatic downgrade from Galaxy -> Slotline when cost-per-minute exceeds threshold or when Galaxy queue lengths exceed safe bounds.

Next experiments (recommended):
- Run same tests on V100 and on compact-quant models to verify quantization shifts cost/latency delta (we did a 4-bit run but need more samples).
- Vary session affinity strength (0.0 to 1.0) to find knee where p99 improves disproportionately to cost.
- Synthetic workload with heavier mobile handshake/slow upload characteristics to measure amplification of tails.
- End-to-end UX sampling: synthetic user-perceived latency (time-to-first-token + steady throughput) and correlation with abandonment in UI flows.

Checklist for follow-ups:
- [ ] Add real customer trace sample (anonymized) to replicate production session mix.
- [ ] Narrow cost model variance: instrument cold KV rebuild cost per model shard.
- [ ] Open an infra perf PR to add a counter for 'affinity-evictions' (link to PR above).

References / Links:
- GitHub PR (runtime affinity experiment): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2847
- JIRA ticket for benchmark orchestration: JIRA-OBS-613
- Slack thread: #obs-session-affinity (see thread pinned messages)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory and deliberately skips tight statistical CI; numbers are median-of-runs to help decide next-phase A/B.
- Please comment with suggestions for additional signal (GPU utilization percentiles, memory pressure traces, decoder stall count).
